q: What is the Dutch CO2 Performance Ladder, and do Indian IT or engineering firms bidding in the Netherlands need it?
title: CO2 Performance Ladder for Indian firms
short: The CO2 Performance Ladder is a Dutch certification, run by the foundation SKAO, that rates how a company measures and cuts its carbon. It is not a legal requirement. Dutch public buyers such as ProRail and Rijkswaterstaat use it in tenders as an award advantage, so you need it only if the tenders you chase give one.
audience: Indian IT services and engineering firms bidding for Dutch public contracts

sections.h: How the Ladder works in a tender
p: The buyer applies a notional discount to your bid price for the Ladder level you commit to, so a certified bidder can win at a higher actual price. Each tender sets the discount per level. You can bid without a certificate; you just compete without that discount. A bidder that claims a level must show it meets it within one year of award, and the tender sets the sanction if it does not.

ul: Handbook 3.1 has five levels, from a measured footprint of your own energy use and travel up to supply chain (Scope 3) work and sector initiatives.

Handbook 4.0, published 14 January 2025, replaces them with steps: internal emissions first, then supply chain engagement, then long-term climate leadership. Three steps are in use and a fourth is being developed.
Certification to version 4.0 has been possible since 14 July 2025; version 3.1 certificates can be issued until 14 January 2027.
The exact requirements sit in SKAO's current handbook.

sections.h: Is it worth it for an Indian firm
ol: List the Dutch tenders you bid for and check how many give a Ladder award advantage.
Decide the organisational boundary: the Dutch entity alone, or Indian delivery centres too, since certification covers what you put inside it.
Price the work: a footprint to the handbook's standard, reduction plans, and an annual audit by a certifying body accredited for the Ladder.
Compare that cost with the discount you would earn on bids you expect to win.

p: Every level starts with a credible Scope 1 and 2 footprint: electricity, DG diesel, company cars and business travel, with source documents. Building that from your bills and travel records is useful for the Ladder and for any other client asking for carbon data.

senseible: Senseible builds a Scope 1 and 2 record from your electricity bills and fuel invoices, with a fingerprint on each file, which you can use as the footprint the Ladder starts from. Ladder certificates are issued by SKAO-accredited certifying bodies after their own audit.
